answers.rationale: For family trips, Maya repeatedly accepts a reasonable nonstop or single-connection premium to avoid long, fragile, or travel-heavy routing. C reaches JAC with a normal single connection and a substantial pre-5 p.m. shuttle buffer. A saves only modestly while imposing a five-hour wait and arriving close to the shuttle cutoff; B adds an unpriced long drive and rental-car friction; D adds two connections.

D is the most approval-ready, fully verified business-stay recommendation: central access, credible work-desk and quiet-room evidence, and breakfast explicitly included on the selected refundable rate. Maya consistently favors reliable commute, workability, and confirmed amenities over more distinctive rooms or nominal breakfast claims. C is attractive but still requires breakfast verification before it can be represented as covered.

The added sign-off ending at 12:45, with possible follow-up questions, makes the approved 3:10 nonstop too brittle after the airport transfer. Maya repeatedly chooses a later same-day nonstop when a client closeout may slip, while rejecting one-stop alternatives that save little. D supplies meaningful local-time and airport buffer without adding a connection; its $68 premium is approvable.

A best balances schedule resilience, nonstop simplicity, and a reasonable return home. The early Monday nonstop protects the required Monday-afternoon arrival, while the 2:55 p.m. nonstop leaves enough time after the 9:45 debrief for the two-hour write-up and a normal airport transfer. D creates an unnecessarily tight post-debrief airport sequence; C starts later Monday and returns later than needed; B saves money but adds connections in both directions.
